Hi,

I'm making my way through the ggvis pages on Rstudio and after this example:

mtcars %>% ggvis(~wt, ~mpg, shape := "cross") %>% layer_points()

I am wondering how I can learn about what other shapes there are then "cross".
Did I miss a manual page on this?

Obviously, I've done some good old trial-but-mostly-error and also noticed that these don't work:
mtcars %>% ggvis(~wt, ~mpg, shape := 1) %>% layer_points() # any number between 1-25 for the usual R symbols
mtcars %>% ggvis(~wt, ~mpg, shape := "k") %>% layer_points() # where "k" is just the character "k"

In other words how do say in ggvis: ggplot(data = mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point(shape = "k")

Thanks,

Richard

cocaine %>%

  layer_histograms(stack = FALSE) %>%

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am trying to create a map using ggvis that interactively updates the fill attribute based on a Shiny input value. However, I am running into three issues:
Integrating ggvis into Shiny: For whatever reason, the ggvis will not show up when I run the Shiny app, though outside of Shiny app, it displays just fine. In case it is relevant, I am using RStudio on a Mac running OS Yosemite 10.10.
Changing fill attribute without redrawing paths: I would like to dynamically change the fill attribute of polygons based on an input value, without re-drawing the paths themselves. This approach is an attempt to reduce running time as I'm mapping 1450 political units and it takes a while to create the base layer.
Changing legend values: The fills are based on a categorical value that essentially cuts a continuous variable (again, to try to reduce running time). I want to customize the color palette as well, but am having trouble using either the parameters in scale_ordinal or add_legend to change the display values of the legend. Instead of labeling each category, I only want to label a string for the first and last as "Low" and "High" respectively.

For a reproducible code example, please see below (also attached). Thanks in advance for helping a Shiny/ggvis newbie!

Jane

SERVER.R

# libraries

    suppressMessages(library(dplyr))

    suppressMessages(library(ggvis))

    library(shiny)

    library(RColorBrewer)

    # create dummy data

    base.long <- c(0, 1, 1, 0)

    base.lat <- c(0, 0, 1, 1)

    test <- data.frame(long = rep(c(base.long, base.long + 1), 3),

        lat = c(rep(base.lat, 2), rep(base.lat + 1, 2), rep(base.lat + 2, 2)),

        order = rep(1:4, 6), group = rep(seq(1:6), 4)[order(rep(seq(1:6), 4))],

        var = rep(seq(5, 30, 5), 4)[order(rep(seq(5, 30, 5), 4))])

    # define color palette

    spectrum <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(n = 4, name="YlGn"))

    shinyServer(function(input, output) {

        # determine fill color based on variable

        toplot <- reactive({

            test$fill.col <- as.character(cut(test$var, seq(10, 30, 5),

            include.lowest = T, labels = spectrum(4)))

            test$fill.col <- ifelse(is.na <http://is.na>(test$fill.col) |

                    test$var < input$range[1] | test$var > input$range[2],

                "#FFFFFF", test$fill.col)

            return(test)

        })

        toplot %>%

            group_by(group) %>%

            ggvis(x = ~long, y = ~lat) %>%

            layer_paths(fill = ~fill.col) %>%

            scale_ordinal("fill", range = c("#FFFFFF", spectrum(4)),

                label = "Variable Value") %>%

            set_options(width = 400, height = 600, keep_aspect = T) %>%

            bind_shiny("test.ggvis")

    })

UI.R

    suppressMessages(library("ggvis"))

    shinyUI(fluidPage(

            sidebarLayout(

                sidebarPanel(

                    sliderInput("range", label = "Filter Range",

                        min = 5, max = 30, step = 5, value = c(5, 25))

                ),

            mainPanel(ggvisOutput("test.ggvis"))

    #         mainPanel(uiOutput("test.ui"), ggvisOutput("test.ggvis"))

        )

    ))
